# driver

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/driver"
```

Package driver owns module compilation.

A module is the unit of compilation because imports, build constraints, and test packages decide which files form a program. The driver keeps those choices consistent across frontend checking and lowering. It uses Go's build rules so TGo files belong to the same packages as their Go equivalents.

Source files are authoritative. Existing generated files can be stale and must not affect source checking. The driver first writes original TGo at generated paths, then replaces it with checked generated Go.

Compilation passes data through these steps: read module files, prepare a generated Go path for each TGo input, select source with Go's build rules, check source packages, lower expressions, and check emitted Go. Each step keeps the data required by the next step.

The driver writes generated Go in the source module. Expression evaluation rules belong to the lowerer.

## func Compile

```go
func Compile(dir string)
```

Compile translates the module's TGo files into Go files in the same module. Invalid source and compiler failures panic.
